title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
description:
# Reverse Nodes in k-Group

Given the `head` of a singly linked list and an integer `k`, reverse the list nodes in consecutive groups of exactly `k` nodes and return the head of the modified list.

If the final group has fewer than `k` nodes, leave those nodes in their original order. You may change only the `next` pointers between nodes; do not change the values stored in the nodes.

The input list itself may contain repeated values, so the operation is about node positions, not about sorting or comparing values.

Example arrays display values in `next` order; `[]` denotes an empty list (`null`). A node stores its value in `val` and its next node in `next`. Use node objects for list parameters and results as shown in the initial code.

## Example 1

**Input:** head = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 2
**Output:** [2,1,4,3,5]
**Explanation:** The groups [1,2] and [3,4] are reversed. The leftover node [5] stays in place.

## Example 2

**Input:** head = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 3
**Output:** [3,2,1,4,5]
**Explanation:** Only the first three nodes form a complete group.

## Constraints

*   The number of nodes in the list is `n`.
*   `1 <= k <= n <= 5000`
*   `0 <= Node.val <= 1000`

solutions.name: Iterative Kth-Node In-Place Reversal
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a dummy node before the list and keep `groupPrev` at the node immediately before the next group. For each round, find the kth node after `groupPrev`. If it exists, reverse all pointers from the group start up to that kth node, then reconnect the reversed group to the previous and next parts of the list.

## Key Insight

The kth node check separates boundary detection from pointer reversal. Once `groupNext` is saved, reversing the group can point each node back toward `groupNext`, so the tail is already connected to the untouched suffix.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n), because each node is visited a constant number of times
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Group Head-Insertion Rotation
solutions.description:
## Approach

After confirming that a full group of `k` nodes exists, keep the first node of the group as `groupTail`. Repeatedly remove the node after `groupTail` and insert it immediately after `groupPrev`. After `k - 1` moves, the group has been reversed in place and `groupTail` is the node before the next group.

## Key Insight

This route reverses the group by local front insertions instead of running a separate pointer-reversal loop. It is the same linked-list invariant as insertion at the front of a small sublist, bounded to one group at a time.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Recursive First Group Reversal
solutions.description:
## Approach

First scan `k` nodes to prove the current prefix is a complete group. If it is not complete, return `head` unchanged. Otherwise reverse the first `k` nodes, recursively process the suffix, and connect the old head, now the tail of the reversed group, to the recursive result.

## Key Insight

Each recursive call owns exactly one complete group. The original head of that group becomes its tail after reversal, which is the only node that needs to be connected to the processed suffix.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n/k) recursion depth

solutions.name: Stack per Complete Group
solutions.description:
## Approach

Read up to `k` nodes into a stack. If a full group was collected, pop nodes back into the result list so the group is appended in reverse order. If the final group has fewer than `k` nodes, append it from its original first node and stop.

## Key Insight

The stack makes the group boundary and reversed order explicit, which is useful for teaching and debugging. The tradeoff is `O(k)` extra storage instead of the constant-space pointer routes.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(k)
